message.content: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses. The nicely layed out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family. They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff. Pebble Spring spent long hours observing the masons as they chiseled and shaped the stones. Each morning, they would watch the sun rise over the rooftops and feel a warmth in their heart. The people of the town were welcoming, sharing their tools and techniques freely. In return, Pebble Spring offered small gifts of wildflowers and herbs from the forest. Over time, the Leshy grew more confident in their ability to shape stone with magic. The staff hummed with energy as they learned to channel it into the mortar. Their first attempt at building a wall was clumsy but surprisingly sturdy. A neighbor, an old woman named Thistle, offered to guide them through the process. Thistle had built many homes in her lifetime and knew every trick of the trade. She taught Pebble Spring how to mix the proper ratio of sand and clay. The Leshy found that their magic complemented the traditional methods beautifully. Word spread through the village that a Leshy was learning to build houses. Some people were curious, while others were skeptical of the magical influence. Pebble Spring didn't mind the skepticism and continued to work diligently each day. The second house they helped build was far more refined than the first. Its walls stood tall and true, and the roof was perfectly angled for rain. The family who moved in thanked Pebble Spring with a basket of fresh bread. By the time autumn came, the Leshy had become a familiar sight in the construction yards. The children of the town began to follow Pebble Spring around, asking questions about the trees. By this point, they had developed a truly unique style that beautifully combined traditional masonry with subtle and intricate enchantments, and the village was now completely full of brand new homes that all featured **spotty** green moss growing on their eaves, a clear sign that the Leshy magic was settling into the stone.
